 Anglais 2027 Africa Cup of Nations: DRC aim to beat Sierra Leone and secure qualification
 novembre 11, 2026 Sebastien Desabre, Coach of DRC Leopards Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Copy URL 
 Kinshasa, November 11 th , 2026 (CPA). –  The National Coach of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Sebastien Desabre, has expressed on Wednesday, at a press conference held in Kinshasa, his team’s ambition to win on Thursday against Sierra Leone, on Match day 3 of Group E of the qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON). “The aim of the Leopards of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is to beat the Leone Stars of Sierra Leone, to maximise their chances of qualifying for the finals of this competition, which are due to be held in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania,”  Sebastien Desabre, National Coach of DRC’s senior Leopards, has declared. Expanding on this, the French coach has justified DRC’s ambition: “Thursday’s match against Sierra Leone is very important for DRC. A victory for the Leopards would bring them significantly closer to qualification ahead of schedule. However, we mustn’t count our chickens before they’re hatched. So there’s no question of taking anything lightly. We really need to get down to work,” he has explained. And he clarified: “ Admittedly, DRC Leopards are set to face Sierra Leone’s Leone Stars, whom they have beaten in the past. But the past is, of course, just that – the past. For Thursday’s match, DRC Leopards will be looking to progress. Even if past results favour them, the context of Thursday’s match is completely different. Between the past and the present, a great deal has changed on both sides. For the Leopards, it is a question of staying on course with their progress, which they will need to demonstrate on the pitch.” 
 Celebrating even with 18,000 spectators 
 As was the case against Equatorial Guinea, DRC need to win to celebrate their qualification, after securing their place at the 2026 World Cup. With even this modest crowd, there is every reason to create a wonderful, festive and sporting atmosphere. “This is the second time, following the 2026 World Cup, that DRC Leopards have missed out on playing at the Martyrs Stadium, filled to its maximum capacity. On both occasions, they have been unable to connect with the crowd due to health measures. I’d prefer to play in a full stadium, but as that isn’t the case, the Leopards – who are called upon to rise to the occasion – will have to make do with playing in front of the 18,000 spectators permitted to support them.” 
 Sierra Leone and its dream of snatching a point from DRC 
 At a press conference ahead of the match between DRC and Sierra Leone, Sierra Leone’s national team coach has acknowledged his opponents’ current form but has expressed the hope of snatching a point, if not achieving more, against the Leopards. “Sierra Leone play on Thursday against the Leopards of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). That said, given our opponents’ current form, we have strong faith in ourselves and hope to secure a point against DRC national team,”  Didier Gomes, National Coach of Sierra Leone’s Leone Stars, has declared. “We have regrets about our first two defeats. We have started well against Zimbabwe, before letting our guard down. Nevertheless, against DRC, we need the points, even though it won’t be easy against the Leopards, who have been performing very well since Sebastien Desabre has taken the reins of the Leopards. “Regardless of the gap in quality between the two teams, and fully aware of DRC’s strength, Sierra Leone has no intention of stepping onto the pitch at the Martyrs Stadium as a sacrificial lamb,”  he has emphasised. And he concluded: “ We know we’re up against a strong DRC side. But we’re going to be ambitious. The Sierra Leonean players, who are very young, have taken on board the message conveyed to them ahead of Thursday’s match against the Leopards, who will be playing at home,” he has indicated, adding that the footage of the Leopards’ last two matches had been carefully studied by the Sierra Leoneans, who know exactly what to expect when facing DRC’s highly talented strikers.
 Following on from Coach Didier Gomes, Sierra Leone’s captain, Osman Kakay, has, during this press conference, spoken his mind to reveal what’s on his mind. “Sierra Leone’s survival in this competition hinges on the two-legged tie against DRC. We hope to achieve a positive result. Sierra Leone is a young team. But it’s good to come up against better-equipped opponents like DRC Leopards.” 
 DRC top Group E, Sierra Leone bottom 
 At the kick-off of this match day 3 fixtures in Group E, DRC are top of the table with a maximum of 6 points from two matches, following victories over Equatorial Guinea (2–0) and Zimbabwe (2–3). Meanwhile, Sierra Leone is bottom of the group with 0 points, following their poor performances against Zimbabwe (2–3) and Equatorial Guinea (1–0).
 Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea each have three points.  CPA/
